Scholars LOVED today's escape room activity.

Hayden is at ELA on Wednesdays. 
Sophia is at band today.
Kristian was very distracting for the other students who were really enjoying the lesson/game.
Our 5th grade scholars adjusted well to our change of venue for this week.  They were quite engaged in our time together today.

Scholars were quite engaged in the lesson today.  I applaud them in adjusting to the change in venue in which we work.  This week is Lori Flemming Elementary's Book Fair which impacted our usual space. Thankfully, the scholars' level of engagement didn't suffer. I was pleasantly surprised.
Xavier notably more alert since the return of his classmate,, Riley.  Good to see a level of energy in him that I hadn't seen before.
Jordan was not willing to participate much today.
It is enjoyable to witness the scholars so engaged in their work.  We are creating words via prefixes and suffixes.  We will further explore the benefits of learning to do so next week.
Riley is back and Xavier is excited.  Well, they both were.  Fun session today.

My scholars LOVED our lesson today about plays/play parts. They were a little louder and rowdier than usual because of the silly voices. Kristian was still refusing to participate and making the lesson a little different.
Scholars unable to complete surveys due to Chromebooks blocked.  Substitute teacher for the class unable to unblock their devices.  Will address tomorrow.
Scholar Riley absent again today, making the session a one-on-one with Xavier once again.

Maurelle and Jayla are more focused on chatting than session work.  During one on one goal setting session, Jayla noted that in order for her to improve in ELA she must 'pay attention.'  Maurelle, appears oblivious even to that concept...I'm considering changing their seating arrangement because they seem to rub off on one another and not for the better...
Again, Xavier was the single scholar in session today.  He seems more confident and relaxed in one on one session...
Xavier seemed to thrive on 1 on 1 basis.  Seemed surer of himself in our session in which he was the only scholar.
We had to complete goal setting sheets one-on-one so the group was restless and Kristian was having problems focusing again.

Scholars were quite animated as we explored The Word Wheel, prefixes & root words in forming new words.  It's exciting for me to see their understanding of forming words and their vocabularies enhanced...

Scholar Riley was in an intrusive mood today.  Not sure how much she absorbed.  We are learning how words are formed.  Although scholar participation is more than welcomed, her manner of participation bordered disruption.  This is new for her, so I'm confident her behavior was due to her having a bad day (better described as having a day more 'challenging' than normal for her).
Hayden refused to come to the tutor session today. I asked numerous times for Hayden to speak with me about what was going on. His teacher called the principal took Hayden to the main office.
All scholars were struggling to focus today. One was also being disruptive throughout the entire lesson.

Surprised to learn scholars had little conception of 'sequences or sequential order.'  I tried relating our current lesson in 'sequence ideas to summarize' to what I thought they knew re sequences in math.  Succeeded in explaining both...

Scholars learned and engaged at their best yet.  The bullets of the article and corresponding activity were positive in revealing how much the scholars learned and were able to identify re the main idea and supporting details of the text.
Kaylee had to do her survey on my computer today because hers died.
Scholar initially stated that he was 'bored' - as always.  However, he was quite engaged in the lesson today.
Power went out in the middle of our lesson.
Scholars were fully engaged from the warm-up to the end of the session...

Both scholars were quite engaged today.  Xavier has not been with us since the beginning of last week (Feb. 3).  His classmate was generous in sharing information with him.  It gave her an opportunity to share with him what she learned, and that aided me in accessing what she understood.

Our scholars are often locked out of parts the school's wifi system that makes accessing Pearl impossible.  This eats into our time between sessions as well as at the end of the day  - such as today...

Scholars were most engaged this session.  They particularly enjoyed the Pictionary and Word games.  They were engaged in the historical piece presented for Black History Month on The History of Hip Hop. We learned together and it was fun.  Jayden, the reserved, almost stoic scholar knew more about this subject than I ever imagined, AND - He did a little rap!
Scholars blocked from Pearl and could not gain access.  Will try to rectify...
Scholars were blocked and could not access Pearl.  Will attempt to rectify...
Wifi system down in school.  Will have scholar complete Pearl survey tomorrow.
Scholars were excited today.  Perhaps it's because it was our only day in class this week due to the snowstorm.  They were eager and quite engaged.
System shut down and scholars were unable to access the survey.
Scholars were motivated and fully engage in discussion of a short story and in identifying the main idea, key words, cause and effect of the story.
Scholars were fully engaged today.  They were focused and ready to work today.  It was probably the best yet...
Scholars were fully engaged and expressed disappointment when the session was over.  Wanted more time...
Scholars were fully engaged an excited about our reading and residual discussion.
Scholars were fully engaged in discussion about "Working Dogs."  Practice test proved reading comprehension was good.
Scholars were fully engaged in the reading and discussion of the article, "Working Dogs."  The practice test was helpful in determining their comprehension of the article, which was positive.
Scholars were fully engaged in discussion and reading the article,  "Working Dogs.'

I think the scholars got off to a good start.  Most of them appeared quite excited for the tutoring experience, despite not truly understanding its significance at this point in their experience of it...

Endeavor to transform the excitement of a new experience into an overall excitement of learning.  Remember that two of the 5th grade scholars said that 'learning' was 'difficult for them.'  Explore ways of alleviating that for them.

I quite enjoyed meeting and getting to know the two scholars - Riley and Xavier.  One was high energy and loquacious, and the other was sedate and reticent.  The experience of the two made for an interesting first encounter - one that left me hopeful and smiling...I expect an addition to the two tomorrow for a class of three scholars...
